Your Attack level is used to determine how likely you are to hit your target in melee combat. A higher Attack level will give you a better chance to hit.
Additionally, a higher Attack level will allow you to wield more powerful weapons. A weapon with a higher Attack bonus will give you more accuracy in combat.
You can select your Attack style from the Combat Options side panel. Different enemies are weaker or stronger against different Attack styles, so choose carefully.

Construction gives you access to your very owned Player-Owned House. To get started, you'll need to buy a house from an Estate agent.
Once you have a house, you'll need to build furniture. Most furniture can be built with planks, which can be obtained via taking logs to a sawmill.
To build furniture, grab a hammer and a saw, enter your house in build mode, select a hotspot and select the furniture you want to build.
As your Construction level increases, you'll be able to build bigger houses, gain access to more kinds of room in your house, and be able to build fancier furniture.
You'll also become able to build better facilities for boats.
Servants can be hired at the Ardougne Domestic Service Agency, north of the marketplace in East Ardougne.

Cooking is a skill that lets you make all kinds of delicious food that will typically restore your Hitpoints, amongst providing other benefits.
At its most basic, Cooking can be done by simply taking raw meats and fish to either a fire or a range. You'll get better results overall if you use a range, though.
Some foods will require you to prepare your ingredients before you can cook them. For example, you first need to mix flour and water into a dough before you can bake them into bread.
As your Cooking level increases, you'll get access to an increasing list of recipes. You'll also find that you accidentally burn your food less of the time as well.

Crafting is a wide-ranging skill that allows you to create various pieces of armour, jewellery, equipment and more.

To craft armour out of animal hides, you'll typically first need to take the hides to a tanner to get them tanned, then combine them with a needle and thread, which can be acquired from certain Crafting shops in the world.

To make pottery, you'll need to obtain some soft clay, obtained by adding water to clay. You can then use a pottery wheel to shape the clay into an unfired item, which you can then finish in a pottery oven.

To make jewellery, you'll need to first get a crafting mould. You can then take that mould and some gold or silver bars to a furnace to craft your jewellery. At higher Crafting levels, you can cut gems and mould them simultaneously to create jewellery, which you can enchant with Magic!

Farming allows you to grow various flowers, vegetables, trees, herbs and more in farming patches across Gielinor.
To get started, you'll need some seeds and a seed dibber, as well as a rake to remove weeds from the patch you want to use.
Once you've cleared the patch, you can add your seed to it. You can also optionally water it with a watering can or add a bucket of compost to decrease the chances of your plant becoming diseased.
It'll take a while for your plant to grow, so feel free to explore the world and come back to it later!
Once your plant has grown, you might need another tool to collect the harvest. For instance, you'll need a spade to dig up potatoes.
If you're worried about your crops becoming diseased, most crops can be protected by the nearby gardeners. They'll usually want you to give them specific produce in payment.
As your Farming level increases, you'll gain access to more crops to grow, as well as obtaining greater yields when harvesting.

Level 23 Farming allows you to make a scarecrow and place it in a flower patch.
Scarecrows ward sweetcorn from being attacked by birds, which helps to prevent disease.

How to make a scarecrow:
1. Fill an empty sack with straw from a bale.
2. Drive the hay sack onto a bronze spear.
3. Place a watermelon on top as a head.
4. Stand the scarecrow in an empty flower patch.

Fletching allows you to create various ranged weapons, as well as ammunition to go with them.
Making bows requires bowstring, which can be made from flax at a spinning wheel. You can use a knife on some logs to carve an unfinished bow, then add the bowstring to complete the weapon.
To create arrows, you'll first need to carve logs into arrow shafts with a knife, then tip the arrow shafts with feathers. Finally, you'll need to add some arrow heads.
To make bolts, you only need to combine unfinished bolts with feathers. You can also chisel gemstones down into bolt tips, with each gemstone being able to top a different bolt.
You must complete the Druidic Ritual quest to unlock the Herblore skill.
Herblore allows you to make potions with herbs and ingredients found across Gielinor.
To make a potion, you first need to clean a grimy herb, then combine it with a vial of water to make an unfinished potion. You can then add the secondary ingredient(s) to complete the potion.
You must undergo barbarian Herblore training from Otto Godblessed before you can make these potions.
In the Chambers of Xeric, potions are mixed in water-filled gourd vials that may be found in the caverns.
Potions will be strong (+), standard or weak (-), depending on your Herblore level.

Hitpoints are used to tell you how healthy your character is. A character who reaches 0 Hitpoints has died, but will reappear in their chosen respawn location (normally Lumbridge).
As with any skill, you will restore 1 missing Hitpoint every minute, but the best way of recovering Hitpoints is by eating food.
If you see any red 'hit splats' during combat, the number shown corresponds to the number of Hitpoints lost as a result of that strike.
Blue hit splats mean no damage has been dealt.
Green hit splats are poison damage.
Teal hit splats are venom damage.
Orange hit splats are disease damage.
Dark purple hit splats are corruption damage.
Dashing kebbit: Restores 23 Hitpoints and 10 Run Energy
Moonlight antelope: Restores 26 Hitpoints and cures 1 level of poison
Anglerfish: Restores Hitpoints based on your Hitpoints level up to a maximum of 22 - can boost beyond your level
Saradomin brew: Restores 15% of your Hitpoints level plus 2 - can boost beyond your level

Regular damage variant shown when you deal your maximum damage.
Most damage hitsplats have a highlighted max hit version.
Boat damage - Shows damage to a boat.

Shield damage - Shows damage to a boss' shield or that a player was protected from an attack.
Example: The Hueycoatl's tail shield.

Armour damage - Shows damage to a boss' armour.
Example: Zalcano's armour.

Poise damage - Shows damage to a boss' poise, usually used to transition a boss to another phase.
Example: The Wardens in the Tombs of Amascut.

Corrosion damage - Deals damage reduced by armour. May also apply a corrosion status effect, dealing damage in regular intervals.
Example: Shellbane gryphon.

Poison - Hitpoint damage dealt in regular intervals, decreasing in potency over time.
Can be cured with an anti-poison effect.

Venom - A more powerful form of Poison.
Can be cured with mutliple anti-poison effects or a single anti-venom effect.

Bleed damage - Hitpoint damage dealt in regular intervals. Some types of bleed are more potent while moving.
Can be cured with an anti-bleed effect.
Example: Custodian Stalkers.

Burn damage - Hitpoint damage dealt in regular intervals. Stacks up to <5>.
Example: Burning Claws special attack.

Disease stat drain - Drains a stat in regular intervals.
Can be reduced/cured with a cure disease effect.
Example: Zogres in Jiggig.

Disease damage - If the stat being drained by an active Disease reaches 1, you start taking Hitpoint damage instead.
Can be reduced/cured with a cure disease effect.

Doom - Shows amount of Doom stacks. A certain amount instantly kills the player.
Example: The Fortis Colosseum Doom modifier.

Healing from certain sources.
Example: The Blood Moon in Neypotzli.

Prayer drain - Shows drain to a player's Prayer.
Example: Frost Nagua in the Ruins of Tapoyauik.

Corruption - Drains Prayer points over time.
Examples: Corruption spells and the Phantom Muspah encounter.

Cold - Drains warmth.
Example: The cold in the Wintertodt encounter.

Charge - Shows something is being charged.
Example: Totems in The Nightmare of Ashihama encounter.

Uncharge - Shows charge is being removed from something.
Example: Totems in The Nightmare of Ashihama encounter.

Alternate charge - Shows something is being charged.
Example: Kephri's shield restore in the Tombs of Amascut.

Alternate uncharge - Shows charge is being removed from something.
Example: Crocodiles draining the Palm of Resourcefulness in the Tombs of Amascut.

Sanity drain - Shows sanity lost form certain sources.
Example: Lost Souls in the Whisperer encounter.

Sanity Gain - Shows sanity gained form certain sources.
Example: Corrupted Seeds in the Whisperer encounter.

Magic grants you access to a wide variety of spells. To cast each spell, you will need a specific set of runes.
Select a spell in this guide to see what runes it requires.

Select a spell on the 'Magic' side-panel to begin casting it.
If a spell is supposed to work on a nearby monster, player or object, you should select the spell, then select the target on which you wish to cast the spell.
Staves can also be used to auto-cast certain offensive spells in combat. To enable this, equip your staff, go to the 'Combat Options' side panel, and select one of the 'Spell' options.
You can use certain pieces of equipment to replace runes in order to cast spells. For instance, an equipped Staff of Air counts as an infinite supply of air runes.
Ancient Magicks are available after completing Desert Treasure I.
Lunar spells are available after completing Lunar Diplomacy.

Mining allows you to get various minerals from the world for use in other skills, primarily Smithing.

To mine a rock, simply interact with it while holding a pickaxe you have the level to use and you'll start mining it. Eventually, you'll collect the ore and the rock will deplete. Low-level rocks will replenish themselves fairly quickly, but higher-level ones will take longer and longer to come back.
At higher Mining levels, you'll have an increased chance of successfully mining a rock. You'll also be able to use more powerful pickaxes, which decrease the amount of time between mining attempts.
Note that while most pickaxes have an Attack level requirement to equip them, you're still able to use them from within your inventory if you have the required Mining level.

The most common way to increase your Prayer level is to offer the remains of the enemies you kill. Burying their bones and scattering their ashes will award you Prayer experience.

Runecraft is the skill that allows you to convert essences into runes, which you can use to cast spells.
To create runes, you'll first need some essence and a talisman of the rune you want to make. You can use the talisman to both locate and access the runic altar, which is where the runes are crafted.
Higher Runecraft levels will allow you to craft more kinds of runes. At higher levels, you'll also be able to make multiple runes per essence.
As your Runecraft skill develops, you become able to craft multiple runes from each piece of essence. You receive experience for each piece of essence crafted, not for each rune crafted.

Pouches come in various sizes which allow you to carry extra essence in them.
As you use the pouches they degrade and store less essence. Speak to the Dark Mage at the centre of the Abyss to restore them.

You must complete the Pandemonium quest to unlock the Sailing skill.

Sailing gives you the ability to captain a boat and sail the seas of Gielinor. Out at sea, you'll find all kinds of things to do. You can salvage shipwrecks for sunken treasure, test yourself in Barracuda Trials, or explore uncharted islands, to name but a few possibilities.
As your Sailing level increases, you'll be able to own more boats, build better facilities on your boats, hire more crewmates, dock at more locations, and much more!

Slayer is a skill that lets you fight increasingly dangerous and lucrative monsters. Some monsters can only be fought if you have a high enough Slayer level.
To get started with Slayer, you'll first need a Slayer task, which can be obtained by speaking to a Slayer Master. You can then kill the assigned target to get Slayer experience.

Once you've completed five tasks, you can start earning reward points. These can be used to skip or block tasks you don't want, or to purchase useful equipment, or to unlock benefits such as extended tasks.

Smithing lets you convert raw ores into useful metals, then use those metals to make your own weapons and armour.
To smelt ores, simply take the mix of ores you need to any furnace and you'll be able to convert them into bars.
Once you have your bars, grab a hammer and take them to an anvil. Bigger items will need more bars to make.
As you advance your Smithing level, you'll be able to make make more gear out of higher quality metals.
To start fishing like a Barbarian, talk to Otto Godblessed when you have at least level 48 Fishing, level 15 Agility and level 15 Strength.
Your Strength level determines your max hit in combat. Whenever you hit your opponent, you will deal a random amount of damage up to your max hit.

Most weapons have a Strength bonus that will also increase your max hit. You can view your Strength bonus (and all of your equipment's stats) by selecting 'View equipment stats' under the Worn Equipment side panel.

Thieving lets you steal items from various people and stalls. Be careful, as people won't take too kindly to you going through their pockets, and might call the guards on you, or may take matters into their own hands.
As your Thieving level increases, the odds of you successfully stealing from your target will increase. You will also gain access to more lucrative targets with more valuable loot.

Woodcutting allows you to chop down trees to obtain logs. Most trees in the game can be chopped down with an axe.
Increasing your Woodcutting level will give you a higher chance of successfully chopping a tree. You'll also gain access to more trees to cut down.

In addition to this, higher Woodcutting levels grant access to more powerful axes, which also increase the chance of chopping trees. Note that you can still use an axe in your inventory if you have the Woodcutting level for it, even if you don't have the Attack level to equip it.
